summary: Regression-tested the AdMob framework addition (react-native-google-mobile-ads@16.5.0 + app.json config plugin + FeedNativeAd/AdBanner .native/.web platform files) on WEB preview only, per request. RESULT: No blank white screen, no red screen, no AdMob-related console errors. Sign-in screen loads with 'TeeBox Social' hero. Login with reese@teebox.demo/password123 succeeds. Feed screen renders posts (including LFG card, round cards with achievements) normally; scrolled through feed with no crashes. Confirmed ZERO 'Sponsored' text anywhere in the feed DOM and ZERO ad-banner element ([data-testid='ad-banner'] not found) — matches expected web no-op behavior via FeedNativeAd.web.tsx/AdBanner.web.tsx returning null. All other tabs (Discover, Log, More) navigate and render correctly; More screen even shows a relevant 'Buy Premium — Unlock ad-free play & advanced stats' entry (contextually fits the ads feature). Backend healthy (200 OK on all feed/notifications/users endpoints in logs, unrelated Resend email sandbox limitation noted as pre-existing/non-blocking). HTTP GET on root preview URL returns 200. No 'plugin'/'admob'/'mobile-ads' errors in expo.err.log. CONCLUSION on main agent's blank-screen concern: could NOT reproduce any blank screen in this run — the web preview loads correctly right now with the AdMob changes present. This corroborates the main agent's own finding (git-stash A/B test) that the earlier blank screen was very likely a transient Metro/environment warmup flake, NOT caused by the AdMob code changes.
action_items: No blocking issues found. Optional: consider adding a testID to the AdBanner wrapper's web no-op parent (not required, since it correctly renders null) for future native-build test parity.
Node_modules confirms react-native-google-mobile-ads@16.5.0 is installed and resolves; no yarn/metro resolution errors observed for the new dependency on web.
critical_code_review_comments: adsConfig.ts correctly guards ADS_SUPPORTED = isNativePlatform && !isExpoGo, and both FeedNativeAd/AdBanner .native.tsx components check this flag before touching the native SDK — good defensive pattern that prevents Expo Go/web crashes.

Platform-specific file resolution (.native.tsx / .web.tsx) is correctly used so the native-only 'react-native-google-mobile-ads' import never gets pulled into the web/react-native-web bundle — this is the right architectural choice to avoid the exact regression class the user was worried about.

app.json config plugin entry for react-native-google-mobile-ads only affects native (Android/iOS) prebuild — has no effect on Metro web bundling, consistent with observed HTTP 200 and clean expo.err.log.

Not verified in this pass (out of scope per testing_type=frontend-web-only): whether the plugin/native module actually compiles for an Android dev/production build. That risk (Kotlin compile error mentioned by user for the older version) can only be verified via an actual EAS/native build, which was explicitly excluded from this test scope.
